subject: NeptunePay urgent: reserved-capacity QPS shortfall, latency and 5xx spike
messages:
From: Anita Rao <anita.procurement@neptunepay.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-20T18:12:00-08:00
Subject: Production spike — 5xx errors + latency on reserved endpoints

Hi Rishi,

We started seeing a severe performance regression this afternoon on our prod endpoints that are pinned to Redwood Dedicated (customer-reserved pool). Between 17:40–18:05 PT we observed a 6x increase in p95 latency (to ~1.6s), error rate spiked to ~4.8% (mainly 502/5xx), and a sustained token QPS increase that appears to exceed our reserved throughput. Attached is a dashboard snapshot and a short log sample showing the 502s.

This is impacting checkout flows; we've throttled client retries to reduce card declines but throughput is still degraded. We have an upcoming marketing push tonight and need this stabilized. Can you confirm root cause and what emergency actions Redwood can take right now? We need an exec-level point of contact.

Thanks,
Anita
Procurement / Ops
NeptunePay

Attachments: neptunepay-dashboard-snapshot-20271120.png, neptunepay-error-sample-502s.log

Subject: Re: Production spike — 5xx errors + latency on reserved endpoints

Folks — I pulled the telemetry from 17:00–19:00 PT and started a quick check against the reserved pool for NeptunePay (reservation id NP-2027-04). Preliminary findings:

- NeptunePay's reserved slot is showing sustained utilization above the committed QPS threshold starting ~17:32 PT. Concurrent token QPS increased by ~4.5x vs baseline.
- We see a burst of KV cache evictions and GRPC queueing on the dedicated nodes serving their reservation; that correlates with the 502 wave.
- No immediate single-model regression on our perf signals; instead it's a capacity vs concurrency problem.

Short-term mitigation I’m executing now (will update):
1) Apply temporary QoS prioritization on the NeptunePay reservation to favor their routes at the network/Egress level (5 min config change).
2) Spin up an emergency burst of 2 additional reserved GPU slots mapped to the same model variant (takes ~7–10 min).
3) Enable aggressive KV prefetch + smaller batch size override for NeptunePay’s route to reduce per-request latency.

I’ve filed INFRA-2147 for the permanent fix; PagerDuty incident PD-98234 is open and I’ve assigned infra on-call. Attaching a short sample of the 502 traces in the ticket.

Ben
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Anita — sorry you’re hitting this. Quick commercial and operational plan while Ben works infra: 

1) We will authorize an emergency burst for NeptunePay: +2 GPU slots for the next 24 hours, effective immediately. No upfront charge; we’ll reconcile with your account team and propose a credit if the root cause is on our side.
2) Ben’s QoS + config changes should reduce the 5xx wave; Ben — please confirm once QoS is in place.
3) Proposed next 90 minutes: run a controlled traffic ramp test with NeptunePay to validate KV/cache behavior and confirm tail latency improvement. Rishi — can you own scheduling the ramp with NeptunePay ops?
4) Naomi will prepare an MOP and add a short-term SLA amendment for tonight’s burst; following stabilization we’ll discuss a longer-term commit adjustment or model-quantization recommendation to avoid recurrence.

We’re scheduling a 30-minute exec bridge at 19:00 PT; Vivek, please join if you can.

Date: 2027-11-21T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: NeptunePay — executive update and approved actions

Anita / Sanjay — quick executive summary and commitments from Redwood: 

- Situation: Between ~17:30–18:05 PT on 2027-11-20 NeptunePay experienced reserved-capacity saturation leading to elevated p95 latency and 5xx errors. Root cause is an unexpected sustained QPS burst that exceeded NeptunePay’s committed reservation and caused local KV eviction queueing.
- Immediate actions taken (completed): QoS prioritization applied to NeptunePay routes; +2 emergency GPU slots spun up and attached to their reservation; aggressive KV prefetch + batch size override enabled. These changes are live; Ben confirmed a reduction in 5xxs in the bridge.
- Short-term remediation: We’ve authorized the 24-hour emergency burst at no charge while we validate stabilization. Naomi will follow up with a short-term SLA amendment and commercial credit proposal should we determine the failure was due to Redwood capacity allocation.
- Follow-ups and timelines: INFRA-2147 (permanent mitigation) and PD-98234 (incident) are active. We’ll run a controlled ramp test tonight (Rishi to coordinate) and provide a post-incident action memo by EOD tomorrow with long-term recommendations (model sizing, quantization guidance, reservation delta).

I’ll stay on the bridge tonight for any exec questions — we want NeptunePay back to normal before the marketing push.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Sales & Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

On behalf of the Redwood team: Rishi, Naomi, Ben
